comments.author: MythosAd
comments.body:
Thanks, this is really helpful.

My motivation for alternating dense/MoE is less about the current MFU gap and more about separation of concerns: dense layers handle common computation, while MoE layers handle specialization. Keeping them as two clean execution patterns seems to leave more room for independent kernel, scheduling, and parallelism optimization, even if MoE kernels improve substantially.

For position encoding, my preference for learned relative PE on local layers + NoPE on global layers is mainly to avoid positional extrapolation entirely. With a fixed local window, the relative-position range never changes as context grows, while global attention stays purely content-addressed. spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Build RiffleEval as a paired long-context evaluation of coherent stream tracking. Each base item keeps the source text, question, answer, distractors, and token budget fixed while changing document chunks from blocked to riffled order. The primary result is the per-item riffle penalty, sliced by foreign-chunk interference count and token distance.

UncheatableEval is a candidate source feed after revision pinning, token-length filtering, license review, and safety filtering. Its current Marin integration is unsuitable: it downloads a stale GitHub fork whose records are capped at 5,000 characters and supplies no questions or evidence annotations. For v0, use frozen natural documents with exact-answer factual overlays; evaluate a filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` subset as one source arm, beginning with English Wikipedia and permissively licensed documents.

## Description

Long-context evaluations such as NIAH often test retrieval of one conspicuous item from a large context. RiffleEval tests whether a model can maintain several ordered information streams whose chunks repeatedly alternate across a 32K–64K prompt, then reconstruct facts within one stream.

For source document \(D_i = [C_{i,1}, \ldots, C_{i,n}]\), generate a legal merge that preserves chunk order within each source. Every chunk receives an opaque, per-example stream ID and ordinal. Questions and evidence annotations are created and verified against the clean document before riffling.

Each base item produces these conditions:

1. Clean target document, for source-task competence.
2. Blocked full context, with the target and distractor documents contiguous.
3. Riffled full context, with identical content and prompt budget.
4. Adjacent-evidence control for multi-evidence items.

The v0 task families are single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration. Cross-stream joins and continuation NLL remain follow-ups.

The proposed context-length and stream-count matrix is not a full Cartesian product. With 4K–8K source documents, 32K supports roughly 4–8 streams and 64K supports roughly 8–16 streams. Larger documents or additional filler semantics would be required to hold stream count fixed while scaling total context. The generator must reject infeasible cells instead of silently repeating or padding sources.

## Hypothesis or Goal

At fixed content and question difficulty, riffling causes a measurable accuracy loss beyond the loss caused by the same blocked distractors. The loss increases with the number of intervening foreign chunks after controlling for absolute token distance. Better long-context checkpoints should move the retention curve toward larger interference counts.

## Status

Background research is complete. No implementation or model run has started.

### Proposed v0

- 250–500 verified base items, expanded into deterministic paired variants.
- 32K and 64K contexts; feasible 4/8/16-stream cells; approximately 512-token chunks.
- Exact short answers with one-evidence and two-evidence overlays.
- Opaque opening and closing markers with tokenizer-balanced random IDs.
- Random and same-domain distractors.
- Native-model score with tools disabled.
- Exact match, per-item riffle penalty, blocked-to-riffled penalty, and retention curves by token distance, interference count, evidence count, and active streams.
- Target-stream extraction and oracle-evidence diagnostics to separate stream selection from reasoning.
- Frozen generator version, seed, source revision/hash, tokenizer, prompt, and structural metadata for every item.

### UncheatableEval corpus decision

Use it as an optional source-discovery and freshness feed. Do not use the published collection as the sole corpus or reuse `experiments/datasets/uncheatable.py`.

The current upstream `-Long` snapshots contain 7,500 records across 15 categories and retain source URL, date, category, `content`, and `untruncated_content`. They provide recent natural interference, but no question, answer, stable ID, evidence span, or hop graph. The dataset card declares no dataset license, and source rights differ by document. AO3 has safety concerns; arbitrary GitHub files need license and secret checks; BBC is a poor redistribution default; PDF extraction can corrupt arXiv text. Freshness only protects models whose training cutoff predates the crawl.

A derived arm must:

- pin the Hugging Face revision and content hash;
- filter on benchmark-tokenizer length, language, quality, and safety;
- record URL, collection date, source category, license, and transformed-text hash;
- begin with English Wikipedia and individually cleared permissive sources;
- exclude BBC and AO3 from v0;
- generate exact-answer overlays and frozen evidence spans against the exact transformed text.

## Background Research Brief

- Effort / stop rule / date: medium; 2026-08-24; stopped when the internal, benchmark, corpus, and contradiction passes no longer changed the v0 recommendation.

### Current Marin context

- #7638 owns RULER integration. RiffleEval should not duplicate its eval harness work.
- #4736 specified the closest reusable data contract: frozen long-document QA items with exact answers, evidence spans, and length bins.
- #7181 found that retained MRCR context reduced final-turn PPL from 21.0855 to 10.4012 at 8,192 tokens. Its extraction PR #7203 closed unmerged, so it is prior evidence rather than current infrastructure.
- #5825 previously built 32K/64K long-document PPL slices; the implementation was later removed by #6633.
- No existing issue or implementation tests repeated switching among several coherent streams.

### External prior art

- [RULER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654) varies context length and task complexity across multi-needle retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, and QA. RiffleEval adds coherent natural streams and a paired blocked/riffled intervention.
- [MRCR/Michelangelo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640) shows that repeated, similar requests and ordinal selection are harder than unique needles. RiffleEval should include similar competing streams and report random/noise floors.
- [NoLiMa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167) shows that lexical overlap makes retrieval easier and normalizes long-context scores to short-context competence. RiffleEval should vary lexical overlap and reject items with weak clean-document accuracy.
- [BABILong](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf) distributes multi-fact synthetic tasks through natural books. RiffleEval adds several foreground streams, explicit stream identities, and the same task before and after structural transformation.
- [LOFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121) found that marker and prompt formatting materially affect retrieval. Marker tokenization and query placement must be fixed or explicitly ablated.
- [UncheatableEval](https://github.com/Jellyfish042/uncheatable_eval) evaluates rolling internet text by NLL. Its freshness method is useful for source discovery; it does not provide RiffleEval annotations.

### Contradiction and shortcut pass

- Random riffles and IDs prevent fixed-order contamination but do not prevent a model from answering public facts from parametric memory. Synthetic counterfactual overlays provide the durable control.
- Opaque IDs expose segmentation but do not prevent keyword search within the target stream. Lexical-overlap and near-neighbor distractor slices remain necessary.
- “Uniform-ish” legal merges do not independently control gap length. Sample examples from explicit interference-count and token-distance strata.
- Marker token lengths can differ across tokenizers and become an unplanned treatment. Balance marker encodings and store their token counts.
- Native QA generation from unannotated documents can admit one-passage shortcuts. Require evidence spans, clean-document verification, and minimal-evidence ablations.

### Recommended next experiments

#### 1. Validate the paired structural signal at 32K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: 100 overlay items, four streams, 512-token chunks; clean, blocked, and riffled conditions on two representative models with different long-context capability.
- Expected signal / falsifier: a nonzero blocked-to-riffled penalty that grows across interference buckets while clean accuracy remains high. Near-zero penalty, floor-level clean accuracy, or prompt-format sensitivity larger than the treatment falsifies the current setup.

#### 2. Add two-evidence integration and 64K

- Minimum experiment / baseline: two controlled facts in widely separated chunks; adjacent-evidence and oracle-extracted-stream baselines; feasible 8/16-stream cells.
- Expected signal / falsifier: two-evidence retention degrades faster than one-evidence retention while oracle extraction recovers most accuracy. Failure of the oracle indicates base reasoning or question-construction problems.

#### 3. Compare source pools

- Minimum experiment / baseline: matched overlays over a pinned filtered UncheatableEval `-Long` arm and one stable, license-cleared long-document corpus.
- Expected signal / falsifier: model ranking and riffle penalty remain stable across source pools. Large domain-specific reversals require a multi-corpus benchmark or removal of the unstable source.

### Source ledger

| Source | Type | Location | Claim used for | Confidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULER | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654 | complexity axes and baselines | high | nearest variable-tracking precedent |
| Michelangelo / MRCR | paper and official code | https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12640 | repeated similar needles and order | high | conversation format differs from riffled documents |
| NoLiMa | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167 | lexical-overlap shortcut and retention normalization | high | single-association retrieval |
| BABILong | paper | https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/c0d62e70dbc659cc9bd44cbcf1cb652f-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf | distributed multi-fact reasoning in natural text | high | one background stream |
| LOFT | paper | https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121 | formatting and identifier sensitivity | high | fixed retrieval corpora |
| UncheatableEval | official repo and dataset | https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jellyfish042/UncheatableEval-2026-07-Long | source schema, freshness, and corpus limitations | high | no dataset-level license or QA annotations |
| Marin #4736 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4736 | QA manifest and evidence schema | high | closed before implementation |
| Marin #7638 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7638 | active RULER scope | high | avoid duplicate harness work |
| Marin #7181 | GitHub issue | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7181 | paired MRCR PPL result | high | extraction PR closed unmerged |

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates: #7638, #4736, #7181, #5825

## Decision Log

- 2026-08-24: scope v0 to paired single-stream exact QA and two-evidence within-stream integration at 32K/64K.
- 2026-08-24: treat UncheatableEval as an optional filtered source arm; reject the current Marin handle and the unfiltered published corpus as the canonical benchmark source.
- 2026-08-24: defer cross-stream joins, continuation NLL, and 128K+ until the primary structural signal is validated.

## Conclusion

Open. Advance to implementation if the 32K pilot produces high clean accuracy, a reproducible blocked-to-riffled penalty, and a stable ordering across source pools and marker templates.

🤖 **Plan:**

**Scope:** analysis only, no PR. This is a new multi-module eval (paired-variant generator, QA/evidence overlays, harness integration, a filtered source arm) with a v0 spec, not a self-contained fix. The v0 definition of done is concrete enough to build against, so this is a decomposition and coordination note for a human before implementation, not a request for more detail.

**What already exists, and where RiffleEval should attach**

- Eval harness: the RULER work in #7638 (branch `nikil/add-ruler-eval`) adds `experiments/evals/evals.py`, `experiments/evals/task_configs.py`, and lm-eval-harness hooks in [`lm_evaluation_harness_evaluator.py`](lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluators/lm_evaluation_harness_evaluator.py). RiffleEval should register as a task through this harness and reuse its vLLM serving path rather than add a parallel runner. - Data contract: #4736 is the closest prior spec (frozen long-doc QA with exact answers, evidence spans, length bins). Reuse its manifest schema for base items instead of inventing one.

**UncheatableEval source arm — coordinate with the open PR**

The proposal correctly rejects the current handle for the benchmark corpus. Note that PR #8646 is already reworking exactly this code: it swaps the stale `ziqing-huang` fork for `Jellyfish042/UncheatableEval-2026-07` pinned at revision `65889535…`, splits the unified Parquet into 15 category subsets, and drops the old 5,000-char normalization path. ## TL;DR

Add a pinned generative OpenAI MRCR task to Marin's served evaluation path and run a bounded smoke against the registered Snowball 67B S3 export. Issue #8701 measured teacher-forced response likelihood; this follow-up requires the model to generate the requested prior response and its nonce.

## Description

Marin's pinned Evalchemy runtime has no working MRCR task. The new task should use OpenAI MRCR revision `f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d`, preserve the dataset's message order, render explicit `User:` and `Assistant:` roles for the base model, and call the completions endpoint. The scorer must return zero when the response omits the nonce, then remove the nonce from both response and gold before applying `difflib.SequenceMatcher`.

The first run should use the existing `snowball` export at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/exports/grug/june-67b-a2b/step-42150/hf-bf16-vllm/d819cbc63780bd86/`. It should select one example from each MRCR length-bin and needle-count cell that fits the server's advertised context, use deterministic greedy decoding, and preserve raw prompts, generations, per-sample scores, prefix-hit rate, and cell coverage.

## Hypothesis or Goal

The shared evaluation launcher can serve Snowball on CoreWeave, execute canonical MRCR generation through Evalchemy, and write scored sample artifacts without a new checkpoint export. A successful smoke establishes the evaluator and serving path needed for the step-141000/156000/157000 checkpoints in #8701.

## Status

Implemented in #8706. Smoke run `20260826-180537-snowball-mrcr-smoke-40df` succeeded across all 12 context-fitting cells with zero Iris failures or preemptions.

## Links

* Paired likelihood experiment: #8701
* Implementation: #8706
* Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d
* Run evidence: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8702#issuecomment-5430184744
* Durable results: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20260826-180537-snowball-mrcr-smoke-40df/results`
* Logbook: none
* W&B Report: none

## Decision Log

* Use the existing Snowball S3 export before exporting the #8701 checkpoints.
* Keep the task definition in Marin and load it through Evalchemy's local task path.
* Use completion-style prompts with explicit role labels because the evaluated checkpoint is a base model.
* Use greedy decoding for reproducible checkpoint comparisons; do not compare the score directly with OpenAI's sampled API results.

## Conclusion

The Snowball export serves real MRCR through the shared CoreWeave path and writes complete scored artifacts, so no additional export work is needed for this checkpoint. Model quality is low: aggregate MRCR accuracy was `0.004714223641098665`, and only 2 of 12 generations passed the exact nonce-prefix gate. The evaluator is ready to use after exporting the step-141000/156000/157000 checkpoints from #8701.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
With the #6095 demonstration, it seems viable to integrate Ray based tooling like deepseek/smallpond without requiring a fork. This would add a distributed analytics engine support to Marin which we're lacking today. (Apache Ballista is a similar project in this area).

It would be nice to add this as an builtin "system service" which is launched by default by Iris at boot - this would allow users to do smaller ad-hoc queries against our data, stats, or logs without starting a new job.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + referenced PR #6095 (fakeray)
- [x] Survey Iris system-service mechanism (`/system/...` endpoint registry, controller boot order)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Post Research + Proposed Approach (no PR — scope > 100 LOC, design choice required)

# Research

Scope is "wire smallpond into Marin as a default Iris system service", which depends on PR #6095 (fakeray) landing first and requires a design decision about what "system service" means here (long-lived shared executor vs. per-query actor cohort). No code exists today; this is a greenfield integration, not a fix.

Prior art / dependencies:
- [#6095](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6095) — fakeray Ray-Core shim on Fray; smallpond end-to-end already demoed (`/rav/sp-bigjob`). Prerequisite — not yet merged, not in the uv workspace.
- [#5861](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5861) — zephyr Dataset reading SQL via DataFusion. Overlapping intent (ad-hoc SQL over data), different layer (Dataset I/O, not a cluster service).

**Relevant code**
- [`endpoints.py#L48`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/endpoints.py#L48) — `/system/...` endpoint registry, currently only `log-server`
- [`controller.py#L570-L573`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L570-L573) — boot-time system-endpoint registration
- [`controller.py#L476-L521`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L476-L521) — `_start_local_log_server` is the template for an in-process bundled system service
- [`service.py#L1656-L1700`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/service.py#L1656-L1700) — `list_endpoints` resolves `/system/*` from the in-memory map

# Proposed Approach (for human review — do not implement until decided)

Open questions to resolve before writing code:

1. **Service shape.** Smallpond is a driver-orchestrated DAG runner, not a long-running query server. Two options:
   - **(a) Persistent SQL gateway**: a `/system/analytics` endpoint that accepts SQL, runs it via smallpond on a shared (preemptible TPU host or CPU) actor pool, returns results. Needs a query frontend, result paging, concurrency/cost limits, auth.
   - **(b) Pre-warmed actor pool only**: Iris boots a small named smallpond/fakeray actor pool; users submit jobs that attach to it instead of paying cold-start. No new RPC surface — just a documented `ray.get_actor("/system/analytics-pool")` handle.

   (b) is much smaller and matches how `/system/log-server` is used (resolve → connect). (a) is what the issue text implies ("ad-hoc queries against our data, stats, or logs without starting a new job") and is closer to Ballista.

2. **What does it actually query?** Issue mentions "data, stats, or logs". Stats/logs are already in finelog/DuckDB ([`controller.py#L495`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L495)) — finelog's `StatsServiceImpl` is already a SQL surface over cluster stats. Smallpond's win is parquet on `gs://`. So the actual gap is "query our parquet datasets" — overlapping with #5861 (DataFusion in zephyr Dataset). We should pick one engine for cross-parquet SQL, not ship both.

3. **Default-on cost.** Booting analytics workers on every Iris cluster (including small dev/test clusters) burns quota. Default-off behind a cluster-config flag is safer; "system service" framing should not mean "always running".

4. **Boot ordering.** fakeray needs Fray actors; Fray actors need the controller scheduling loop ([`controller.py#L532`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L532)) and a worker pool. The controller boots before any worker. The "system service" cannot literally start in the controller process the way `log-server` does — it needs the autoscaler to bring up its workers first. This is a real lifecycle wrinkle.

Suggested minimal first step (if approved): land (b) — a config-gated `/system/analytics-pool` registered after autoscaler bootstrap, exposing a pre-warmed fakeray actor pool. Defer (a) until there is a concrete user demanding the RPC surface. Coordinate with #5861 owner on engine choice before writing either.

Blocking on: maintainer decision on (a) vs (b), engine-choice alignment with #5861, default-on policy.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
We want to make it easier to write flexibly scheduled jobs to take advantage of whatever hardware resources are available. 

Iris already allows users to manually specify a set of TPUs hardware they can run on, e.g. `or(tpuv5p-8, tpuv6e-16)`, but this requires manually identifying the hardware you want to run on, and is difficult to use properly.

We want to instead introduce device-agnostic scheduling constraints for accelerator _resources_, and use those by default for job-scheduling. This should provide enough structure for users to exclude devices that are technically correct but would have deeply pessimal performance (v5e-128 vs v5p-8).

Straw-man configuration might look something like:

```python
JobConfig.with_tpu(
  hbm="128g",
  flops_per_chip="100t",
  max_chips=32,
  max_vms=4,
)
```

This provides enough information for Iris to identify an appropriate set of TPU topologies which can satisfy this job, while preventing going way off the users desired setup.

Levanter/JAX by default infer the topology so they should work today without modification, though users may want to adjust model parameters (EP/MP/FSDP) based on the physical topology. Ideally we can auto-configure reasonable values by default.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and skill docs
- [x] Surveyed existing constraint/topology code
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR/issue found)
- [x] Post research + proposed approach
- [ ] Await human review before implementation (scope > 100 LOC, multi-module, new API)

**Research**

Today users hard-code a `device-variant` (`TpuDevice.variant`), and Iris already supports an `IN`-style multi-variant constraint that gives the requested `or(v5p-8, v6e-16)` behavior — but only at the granularity of named slices. The topology table at [`tpu_topology.py#L27-L71`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/tpu_topology.py#L27-L71) carries `chip_count / host_count / vm_count / chips_per_vm`, with **no per-chip HBM or FLOPs**, so there is nothing for a resource-style request to match against. The validator at [`constraints.py#L718-L795`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L718-L795) already enforces that all candidate variants share `vm_count` and `chips_per_vm` (the VM is indivisible), which constrains how a resource-based request can be expanded.

**Relevant code**
- [`tpu_topology.py#L17-L71`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/tpu_topology.py#L17-L71) — `TpuTopologyInfo` table; needs HBM/FLOPs fields
- [`types.py#L424-L453`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L424-L453) — `tpu_device(variant, count)` factory; only entry point today
- [`types.py#L505-L534`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L505-L534) — `ResourceSpec`; needs a resource-style constructor
- [`constraints.py#L354-L375`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L354-L375) — `device_variant_constraint([...])` builds the `IN` constraint used as `or(...)`
- [`constraints.py#L718-L795`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L718-L795) — `validate_tpu_request`; alternatives must share `vm_count` and `chips_per_vm`
- [`types.py#L697-L729`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L697-L729) — `adjust_tpu_replicas`; auto-fans replicas by `vm_count`

**Proposed approach**

Resource-style scheduling is a thin shim over the existing variant-IN mechanism. Three changes, in order:

1. **Extend the topology table.** Add `hbm_bytes_per_chip: int` and `flops_per_chip: float` (bf16 peak) to `TpuTopologyInfo`. Source values from the public docs links already cited above each family. Keep them on the variant rows so the topology table stays the single source of truth.

2. **Add a `TpuRequest` dataclass.** Per AGENTS guidance against `default_*` wrappers and boolean dispatch, model this as a real dataclass:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TpuRequest:
    min_hbm_per_chip: int    # bytes; parse "128g" at construction
    min_flops_per_chip: float
    max_chips: int
    max_vms: int | None = None
    families: tuple[str, ...] = ()   # optional allowlist: ("v5p", "v6e")

    def candidate_variants(self) -> list[str]: ...
```

`candidate_variants()` filters `TPU_TOPOLOGIES` by the four constraints, then groups by `(vm_count, chips_per_vm)` and returns the largest group whose chip count is <= `max_chips`. Grouping is required because `validate_tpu_request` rejects mixed VM shapes.

3. **Wire it into job submission.** Add `ResourceSpec.with_tpu(request: TpuRequest)` (or `JobConfig.with_tpu(...)` per the straw-man) that:
   - picks a primary variant (smallest in the candidate set) for `TpuDevice.variant` so `chips_per_vm` is populated for `adjust_tpu_replicas`,
   - sets `device.tpu.count = chips_per_vm`,
   - emits a `device_variant_constraint(candidates)` attached to `IrisClient.submit_job(..., constraints=...)`.

No controller-side changes are required: the scheduler already matches `device-variant IN [...]`, and `validate_tpu_request` already rejects bad expansions.

**Open design questions before I implement**

1. **FLOPs units / dtype.** Pick one canonical metric (bf16 peak, dense, per chip). Tentative values: v4 ~275 TF, v5e ~197 TF, v5p ~459 TF, v6e ~918 TF. Per-chip + `max_chips` is simpler than aggregate `min_total_flops` — agree?
2. **API surface.** `ResourceSpec.with_tpu(TpuRequest(...))` (composable, dataclass-first) vs `JobConfig.with_tpu(hbm=..., flops_per_chip=..., max_chips=..., max_vms=...)` (matches the straw-man, more discoverable). Lean dataclass; want the straw-man kwargs form as a thin wrapper?
3. **Auto-topology hints to Levanter.** Issue says "ideally auto-configure EP/MP/FSDP". That is a Levanter-side mesh inference concern; suggest deferring out of this PR — Iris just narrows the candidate set, Levanter infers mesh at runtime.
4. **Default when no constraints are given.** Should an unannotated training job get a model-aware default (`min_hbm_per_chip >= params * dtype / dp`)? Probably out of scope until we have a model-aware helper.

Estimated size: ~150 LOC across `tpu_topology.py`, `types.py`, plus tests in `lib/iris/tests/`. Will open a PR once #1 and #2 are decided.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description

Follow-up from #5815. The BF16 B200 baseline/profile goal is complete, but the fair-fit d5120/L8 result shows Grug still trails the Megatron TE + flash + native DeepEP profile after the attention-specific work landed.

Relevant #5815 numbers:

| run | profile-window tok/s | post-profile tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Grug d5120/L8, `ragged_all_to_all` | 14,068.57 | 14,230.55 |
| Grug d5120/L8, ring/all-gather comparator | 24,007.82 | 24,350.55 |
| Megatron d5120/L8, TE + flash + native DeepEP | 86,197.25 | 91,574.88 |

The ring/all-gather comparator is about 1.71x faster than `ragged_all_to_all`, so `ragged_all_to_all` is a real bottleneck. It is not the whole gap: the best Grug comparator remains about 3.76x below the Megatron post-profile throughput.

## Scope

B200 BF16, d5120/L8, EP=8, batch=8, seq_len=4096. This issue should focus on Grug MoE transport/combine and the whole-step effects of the transport choice. Attention-only work is tracked separately in #6039 and was integrated through #6059/#6069.

## Definition of Done

- Identify the Grug MoE transport/combine wall-time contribution for the d5120/L8 B200 profile cell.
- Compare `ragged_all_to_all`, ring/all-gather, and any candidate DeepEP-equivalent or fused transport path on the same shape.
- Land only the smallest scoped implementation or harness change needed to make the candidate path reproducible.
- Post before/after post-profile tok/s and profile-window tok/s with artifact links.
- State the remaining gap to the Megatron d5120/L8 profile after the transport change.

## Links

- Parent baseline/profile closeout: #5815
- Existing dispatch/combine issue: #5609
- Existing local GMM/MLP epic: #5328

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue, parent #5815, sibling #5609, AGENTS.md, fix-issue skill
- [x] Inventory existing transport backends and DeepEP plumbing
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PRs targeting this; #5609 is related kernel-replacement work, not overlapping)
- [x] Post Research + Proposed Approach for human review
- [ ] Implementation requires B200 hardware + profiles — handoff to human

# Research

Three Grug EP backends already live in [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe), selected via `implementation=` in [`grug_moe.py#L208-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L208-L215). Per #5815, `ragged_all_to_all` lands at 14.2k tok/s on d5120/L8 B200, `ring` at 24.4k tok/s, vs Megatron TE+DeepEP at 91.6k tok/s. The DeepEP backend exists in Grug ([`ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py)) and has SM100/B200 build paths wired in [`availability.py#L35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/kernels/deepep/availability.py#L35) and [`#L213`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/kernels/deepep/availability.py#L213) but **does not appear in the #5815 results table** — the gap to Megatron may largely be that the Grug DeepEP path has not been measured/optimized for d5120/L8 yet.

**Relevant code**
- [`grug_moe.py#L199-L243`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L199-L243) — EP backend dispatch (ring/raa/deepep) under shard_map
- [`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py) — current default; two `jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all` per layer + repermute
- [`ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py) — DeepEP intranode dispatch/combine; calls `deepep_dispatch_intranode` / `deepep_combine_intranode`
- [`ep_ring.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py) — all-gather + psum-scatter; the 1.71x faster comparator
- [`_moe/common.py#L31`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/common.py#L31) — `_EP_MOE_IMPLEMENTATIONS = (\"ring\", \"ragged_all_to_all\", \"deepep\")`

# Proposed Approach

Why this is not a self-contained fix: closing the gap requires (a) running the existing Grug `deepep` backend on B200 at d5120/L8/EP=8 with the validated DeepEP commit `7febc6e25`, (b) producing JAX/Perfetto profiles, (c) likely 1–N rounds of kernel/layout work on whichever path wins. None of (a)/(b)/(c) is reachable from CI; the issue's Definition of Done is built around B200 throughput numbers.

Suggested ordering for whoever picks this up (in priority order, smallest scope first):

1. **Measure first, code second.** Run the existing `implementation=\"deepep\"` Grug path on the same d5120/L8 cell pinned in #5815 with `DEEPEP_CUDA_ARCH=sm_100` and `DEEPEP_SRC_ROOT` at the validated commit. If it materially closes the gap, the only remaining work may be wiring it as the default for B200 + a runbook entry; that is a true small PR. The fair-fit table in #5815 not listing the `deepep` Grug cell is the central missing data point.

2. **If `deepep` underperforms vs Megatron's native DeepEP, profile to attribute the gap** between three buckets: (i) FFI launch / Python-side packing in `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` ([`ep_deepep.py#L43-L77`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py#L43-L77)) — note this uses `top_k(assignments)` + `take`, which is exactly the scatter/gather pattern flagged in #5609; (ii) intranode CUDA kernel time; (iii) the `segment_sum` collapse in `_collapse_deepep_local_assignments`. The packing/collapse layer is the most likely Grug-side hot path and is a JAX-only fix (no CUDA).

3. **Whole-step effects of transport choice.** The issue explicitly asks for whole-step, not just transport, deltas. The `ring` backend keeps tokens replicated globally and uses `psum_scatter` ([`ep_ring.py#L109-L113`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L109-L113)), trading memory for kernel simplicity — at d5120/L8/EP=8 this works because tokens-per-shard fits, but it will not scale to larger EP. Land the per-transport measurement table before optimizing further so the choice is grounded.

4. **Harness change (smallest landable piece).** A reproducible harness that runs the three backends back-to-back on the d5120/L8 shape and writes the throughput table + Perfetto artifacts. This is the one piece that could land independently as a small PR; it would unblock everyone else and matches the \"smallest scoped implementation or harness change\" wording in the DoD. Likely lives next to existing Grug profile scripts (none found in `experiments/`; check internal scripts).

I have not opened a PR. The actionable next step needs a human with B200 access to either run the `deepep` Grug measurement or to scope the harness PR — I can author the harness PR if pointed at the existing profile-driver entry point used for the #5815 runs.

comments.body:
🤖 # Current result

The d5120/L8 8x B200 Grug run now reaches the #6139 target in post-profile throughput. Megatron reference from #5815 is `91,574.88 tok/s`, so the 10% band threshold is `82,417.39 tok/s`; remote scheduler job `56618` measured Grug ring + `gpu_fa4_thd` + one outer optimizer global clip at `82,622.24 tok/s` normal post-profile and `82,867.95 tok/s` lean post-profile.

Profile-window medians are lower (`79,875.59 tok/s` normal, `80,179.68 tok/s` lean), so I am treating post-profile as the fair comparison, matching the #5815 table convention.

# Component evidence

Remote scheduler job `56575` measured Grug DeepEP fixed-route expert at `0.018508s` / `1,770,473.99 tok/s` for `moe_expert_only_fixed_routes`; the profile artifact is `jax-profile-step-0-2`, though its summary is sparse because the profiler rejected the `device_tracer_level` option. Remote scheduler job `56617` measured ring/ragged-dot A/B: Triton `moe_mlp_block` `0.009495s`, Triton fixed-route expert `0.008371s`, XLA `moe_mlp_block` `0.023439s`, and XLA fixed-route expert `0.022145s`. Remote scheduler job `56618` produced normal and lean full-step `jax-profile-step-6-14` profile artifacts plus `ring_thd_full_step_summary.json`.

# Conclusion

The ranked gap is now: (1) DeepEP is not the winning Grug transport on this shape; fixed-route DeepEP is about 2.21x slower than ring+Triton fixed routes, so do not switch #6139 to DeepEP. (2) The XLA ragged-dot fallback is a large local GMM regression, about 2.6x slower than Triton for the same ring path. (3) Attention + current ring/Triton MoE is sufficient for the whole-step post-profile target; no step-parts follow-up is needed for #6139.

Landing PR: #6160. That PR moves Grug MoE AdamH clipping from per-group clipping to one outer global clip around `multi_transform` and keeps the DeepEP named scopes used for attribution.

spillover_issues.author: ahmeda14960
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Tracking issue filed per dlwh's review comment on #4637 (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/adaptor/lora.py`).

## Problem

LoRA currently excludes `lm_head` by default — `LoraConfig.exclude_modules` defaults to `["lm_head"]`. Every model's `get_lm_head()` accesses `self.lm_head.weight` directly, which breaks when `lm_head` is a `LoraLinear` (it has no `.weight`; the base weight lives at `.wrapped.weight`). `resize_vocab()` makes the same `.weight` assumption.

## Proposed fix

Update `get_lm_head()` in all model classes (`llama`, `qwen`, `gemma`, `mixtral`, `olmo`, `olmo3`, `apertus`, `mistral`) to handle `LoraLinear`, e.g.:

```python
if isinstance(self.lm_head, LoraLinear):
    return self.lm_head.wrapped.weight
```

and fix the same `.weight` assumption in `resize_vocab()`. Then `lm_head` can be dropped from the default `exclude_modules`, enabling LoRA on `lm_head` (which some research suggests is beneficial — Thinking Machines 2025, "apply LoRA to all weight matrices").

## Acceptance

- `get_lm_head()` and `resize_vocab()` handle `LoraLinear` across all listed model classes.
- A model loraized with `lm_head` included passes forward / merge / HF export.
- `lm_head` removed from the default `exclude_modules` (or documented why it must stay).

## References

- #4637 review comment (dlwh) on `lib/levanter/src/levanter/adaptor/lora.py`.
- The `TODO(IMPORTANT)` next to `exclude_modules` in that file.

🤖 ## Goal

Establish an LR scaling law for the MuonH May Recipe of the form

```
LR = m · tokens^(−a) · hidden_dim^(−b) · batch_size^(0.5)
```

so that follow-up experiments (gate 1 / gate 2 ablations) can be launched at the heuristic-optimal LR rather than re-sweeping at every (dim, R).

## Sweeps launched so far

| Sweep group (wandb) | Hidden dim | R (TPP) | LR multipliers | Batch | TPU | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-sweep` (main 4-size grid) | 512 | 4, 10, 20, 60, 120, 240 | 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 | 32 | v5p-? | 30 finished / 30 |
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-sweep` | 768 | 4, 10, 20, 60, 120, 240 | 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 | 64 | v5p-? | 23 finished / 5 crashed / 2 running |
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-sweep` | 1024 | 4, 10, 20, 60, 120, 240 | 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 | 128 | v5p-? | 15 finished / 13 crashed / 2 running |
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-d1280-sweep` (incl. R=120/R=240 resubmit) | 1280 | 4, 10, 20, 60, 120, 240 | 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 | 256 | v5p-32 | 25 finished / 3 crashed / 2 running |
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-tpp5k-d512-d768-sweep` | 512 | TPP=5000 | 0.2, 0.6, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5 | 256 | v5p-32 | 5 running |
| `muonh-may-recipe-lr-tpp5k-d512-d768-sweep` | 768 | TPP=5000 | 0.2, 0.6, 1.0, 1.5 | 512 | v5p-32 | 3 running / 1 missing |

Total: ~150 runs (R values × LR multipliers × dim).

## Current fit (using cells where all 5 lr_mults finished)

Excluded from the fit: (d=512, R=4), (d=768, R=4) — bowls extrapolate above lr_mult=1.6. All cells with any non-finished run are also dropped.

```
LR = 26.9 · tokens^(−0.395) · dim^(−0.121) · batch_size^(0.5)
```

R² = **0.996** on 17 fit points. See `experiments/grug/moe/may_recipe_lr_law_fit.png` and `experiments/grug/moe/may_recipe_lr_sweep_grid.png` (per-cell sweep grid).

## Next

- Wait for in-flight d=768/1024/1280 cells to clear so we can re-evaluate with more data points.
- TPP=5000 sweep adds two longer-trained points (d512 bs=256, d768 bs=512) — primarily to extend the tokens axis and check that the −0.395 exponent holds under longer training at fixed dim.

## Heuristic change (`experiments/grug/moe/heuristic.py`)

Fit form (muonh LR, after `adamh_ratio · adam_lr`):
```
muonh_lr = 26.9 · tokens^-0.395 · dim^-0.121 · batch_size^0.5
```

## Predicted muonh_lr at the README compute-optimal points

| Point | bs | tokens | Old muonh_lr | New muonh_lr | New/Old |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| d512 / 2.19e17 | 32 | 8.37e8 | 0.01245 | **0.02138** | **1.72×** |
| d768 / 1.70e18 | 64 | 2.71e9 | 0.01090 | **0.01810** | **1.66×** |

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 Correction: previous fit had a units bug

The earlier post (`lr = 26.9 · tokens^-0.395 · dim^-0.121 · bs^0.5`) used an `_active_params` formula in the fit script that set `intermediate_dim = d * 4`, while the actual `MoeAdamHHeuristic.build_model_config` uses `intermediate_dim ≈ d/2`. So the `tokens = R · p_active` fed to the regression were ~4× too large. With `tokens^-0.395`, that inflated the coefficient `m` by ~`4^0.395 ≈ 1.74×` to compensate.

## Corrected fit

```
muonh_lr = 18.31 · tokens^-0.395 · dim^-0.150 · bs^0.5    (R² = 0.996, 17 fit cells)
```

(`tokens_exp` unchanged at -0.395; `dim_exp` -0.121 → -0.150; `m` 26.9 → 18.31.)

## Verification

Per-cell `new_pred / old_base_lr` should equal observed `opt_lr_mult`:

| d | R | observed `opt_mult` | corrected `new/old` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 10 | 1.199 | 1.146 |
| 512 | 20 | 1.032 | 1.059 |
| 512 | 60 | 0.904 | 0.935 |
| 512 | 120 | 0.849 | 0.864 |
| 512 | 240 | 0.811 | 0.799 |
| 768 | 10 | 1.106 | 1.113 |
| 768 | 20 | 1.036 | 1.028 |
| 768 | 60 | 0.921 | 0.908 |
| 1024 | 10 | 1.029 | 1.071 |
| 1024 | 20 | 0.947 | 0.990 |
| 1280 | 10 | 1.036 | 1.052 |
| 1280 | 20 | 0.943 | 0.972 |
| 1280 | 60 | 0.858 | 0.858 |
| 1280 | 120 | 0.817 | 0.793 |

Matches within ~5% across the included cells (vs 1.7–2.2× overshoot before).

## Compute-optimal-point predictions (vs old recipe)

| Point | Old muonh_lr | New (corrected) | new/old |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| d512 / 2.19e17 | 0.01245 | 0.01214 | 0.98× |
| d768 / 1.70e18 | 0.01090 | 0.01016 | 0.93× |
| d1024 / 9.00e18 | 0.01078 | 0.00967 | 0.90× |
| d1280 / 2.83e19 | 0.01178 | 0.01032 | 0.88× |

So at compute-optimal the new recipe is **slightly below** the old — consistent with the observed `opt_mult ≈ 0.95–1.05` at low-R cells. The earlier "1.6–1.7× bump" claim was an artifact of the units bug.

## Heuristic update

`experiments/grug/moe/heuristic.py` will be updated to:
```
lr_coeff: float = 0.06602   # was 0.09700 (buggy), original 0.025469
lr_tokens_exp: float = -0.395
lr_dim_exp: float = -0.150   # was -0.121 (buggy), original -0.3678
```

(`adamh_ratio = 13/3` unchanged.)

The compute-optimal runs kicked off in `/larry/iris-run-job-20260526-174529` were running with the *buggy* (~1.7× too high) LR — those will be killed and resubmitted with the corrected heuristic.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This epic tracks the attempt to make Grug's local MoE expert MLP path fast by adapting SonicMoE ideas into a JAX-callable Marin backend. The investigation narrowed from broad Sonic/QuACK custom-call options to the local grouped `w13` / activation / grouped `w2` path and gather/combine behavior on GH200/H200-class GPUs. By mid-May 2026, plain JAX/Pallas paths had shown useful forward performance but not enough backward/remat improvement; the production-facing direction then narrowed to PR #5718's `implementation="sonic"` backend, which keeps existing JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs and ports Sonic's token gather/combine kernel through `jax-triton` with a custom VJP. The remaining work is to validate that backend in realistic GPU training shapes and keep the more fragile CuTe/QuACK ragged-TMA experiments as research notes, not default production dependencies.

### Helpful links
- Latest production-path update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484868494
- PR #5718 scope update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484780037
- jax-triton train-step comparison: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4449166706
- CuTe/QuACK ragged-TMA reproducer result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4453791007
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Goal

Produce and land a local MoE kernel backend for GH200/H200-class NVIDIA GPUs that materially improves Grug's local expert MLP path on the authoritative GPU benchmark cells, with a clear interface boundary against the transport layer.

Success target for this research thread: find a JAX-callable path, or a custom-call path usable from JAX, that gets within roughly 10-20% of Sonic/QuACK on the local MoE block.

## Scope

In scope:
- local grouped `w13` / activation / grouped `w2` path
- local gather-and-sum / combine behavior
- activation-memory-efficient local backward bookkeeping where it matters
- Pallas, Mosaic GPU, custom-call, or direct Sonic/QuACK wrapper routes that can be called from JAX
- comparisons against `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`

Out of scope:
- DeepEP-equivalent dispatch/return transport
- ring vs `ragged_all_to_all` transport design
- broad PyTorch interop layers unrelated to a measured local-kernel win
- router/top-k redesign unless a local kernel requires a narrowly scoped metadata change

## Current Baseline

Primary GH200 shape: `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, `topk=2`, BF16.

| Measure | Real Sonic/QuACK | Best JAX/Grug path so far | Gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| forward | `1.260ms` | `1.285ms` | `+2.0%` |
| `fwd_bwd` | `3.428ms` | `4.035ms` | `+17.7%` |
| `fwd2_bwd` proxy | `4.428ms` | `5.640ms` | `+27.4%` |
| `remat_bwd` / checkpoint | `4.798ms` | `5.844ms` with `prevent_cse=True` | `+21.8%` |

Interpretation:
- Use `fwd_bwd` for ordinary no-remat training comparisons.
- Use `remat_bwd` with `prevent_cse=True` for honest forced-recompute comparisons.
- Do not use the older JAX `remat_bwd=4.056ms` number for parity claims; that used `prevent_cse=False` and appears to have benefited from XLA CSE/reuse across the checkpoint boundary.

## Latest Update

Latest issue comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4484868494

Latest local logbook entries:
- `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-jax-triton-overhead.md`: raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine train-step probes
- `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`, `SONIC-PALLAS-044`: CuTe DSL JAX integration smoke and follow-up ragged-TMA blockers

Local handoff: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`

## Decision Log

- 2026-04-30: narrowed the broad SonicMoE scout to this local-compute epic for Grug MoE GMM/MLP.
- 2026-05-10: Pallas unpack-backward VJP produced a small real training win, about `2.8%` end-to-end on the 006a-style 1x GH200 synthetic run.
- 2026-05-11: full forward path is close enough to Sonic; the remaining question moved to full-block backward and remat behavior.
- 2026-05-12: direct Mosaic GPU vector-indexed metadata/gather path hit JAX lowering blockers; scalar Mosaic workaround lowered but did not close the Sonic gap.
- 2026-05-13: full-block comparison shows best JAX no-remat path is `+17.7%` vs Sonic, but honest remat is `+21.8%` vs Sonic.
- 2026-05-13: naive activation+W13 Pallas/Triton fusion was rejected. It avoids materializing `d_w13_out` but recomputes the SwiGLU derivative across many matmul tiles and runs at `29.361ms` vs `1.836ms` for the materialized baseline.
- 2026-05-13: pure JAX whole-local-MoE `custom_vjp` scaffold was rejected as a speed path. It is locally correct and useful as an ABI scaffold, but full-shape GH200 timing was `12.804ms fwd_bwd` and `14.430ms remat_bwd`, far slower than `sonic_xla`.
- 2026-05-13: Sonic/QuACK down-projection backward bridge succeeded on GH200. JAX-owned tensors via zero-copy DLPack ran the down-backward bucket at `1.008ms` for the full shape, making it a credible custom-call target rather than a production bridge by itself.
- 2026-05-13: CuTe DSL through `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call` succeeded on the GH200 worker (`max_abs=0`, `0.118ms` steady for a vector-add smoke), so the source-level CuTe/JAX port path is available.
- 2026-05-14: raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine with a custom VJP beat the XLA combine proxy in a train-step-shaped GH200 harness, but the QuACK/CuTe down-backward path hit `Unexpected index` lowering failures.
- 2026-05-19: PR #5718 was narrowed to production-visible `implementation="sonic"`: existing concat W13 layout and JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs, plus raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine. CuTe/QuACK dependencies and pseudo-Sonic XLA/down-gather public backends were removed from that PR.

## Negative Results Index

- Full W13 custom VJP around the expert-padded path was too broad and slow; the narrower unpack-backward VJP was the useful part. See https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4416373304 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4416387690.
- Isolated gather/sum Pallas Triton variants, including faithful source ports and inline PTX arithmetic, did not match real Sonic. The remaining gap persisted even in a standalone Marin-free repro and showed worse SASS/register/control-instruction characteristics for Pallas.
- Directly launching the exact Sonic Triton cubin through JAX FFI worked functionally but carried an approximately fixed `56-60us` launch tax, erasing the Sonic advantage for the isolated gather/sum kernel.
- Mosaic GPU high-level vector indexing currently hits JAX lowering blockers for the relevant metadata/gather forms. Scalar `plgpu.load` workarounds lower but are tied-to-slower than Pallas Triton and remain slower than real Sonic.
- JAX checkpoint/remat with `prevent_cse=False` gave a misleading `4.056ms` result. With `prevent_cse=True`, the best JAX remat path is `5.844ms`.
- Naive activation+W13 fusion in Pallas/Triton is a dead end for this shape: fused `dx` and `dw` subkernels are `14-15ms` each because they recompute the activation derivative per matmul tile.
- Pure JAX whole-MoE `custom_vjp` does not improve schedule quality by itself. The corrected scaffold ran `12.804ms fwd_bwd` and `14.430ms remat_bwd`; making W2 transposes explicit was worse.
- QuACK/CuTe ragged TMA is fragile in this integration. The d-gated epilogue has a two-extra-dim encoding workaround, but the production PR removed the CuTe/QuACK dependency path rather than relying on it.

## Current Conclusion

Forward-only performance and isolated combine microbenchmarks are no longer the main decision point. The practical production path is the narrowed `implementation="sonic"` backend from PR #5718: concat W13 layout, existing JAX `ragged_dot` grouped GEMMs, and raw Sonic jax-triton gather/combine with a custom VJP. The CuTe/QuACK custom-call route remains useful research context but is too fragile for the current production PR. Next work should validate the sonic backend on real GPU training shapes and resolve any remaining robustness issues before treating it as a default MoE path.

- SonicMoE repo: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/sonic-moe
- Active research branch: `codex/sonic-equivalent-pallas`
- Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`
- Handoff doc: `/Users/dlwh/src/marin/scratch/moe-block-decomposition-handoff-20260513.md`
- Related replacement issue: #5609

comments.body:

# Scope

Research scouting (multi-session, design-heavy) — no PR opened per agent rules. Output is a paper-to-code map and a proposed first benchmark tranche on top of the kickoff in [#5328 (comment)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5328#issuecomment-4355849477).

# Paper-to-code map (SonicMoE claim → Grug call site)

Source: [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py).

- **gather-fused grouped GEMM**
  - site: [`grug_moe.py#L102-L108`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L102-L108) materializes `x_sort = x[token_ids_sort]` before [`grug_moe.py#L131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L131) `ragged_dot(x_dispatch, moe_w13, group_sizes)`
  - JAX-portable variant: pass `(x, token_ids_sort, group_sizes)` to a gather-fused wrapper around `ragged_dot` so `x_sort` is never materialized. Pure-JAX first; only escalate to Pallas/custom-call if XLA refuses to fuse.
- **activation-memory growth in backward**
  - dominators: explicit checkpoints at [`L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L128) (`grug_moe_dispatch_input`, `T*K*D`), [`L131`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L131) (`grug_moe_expert_hidden`, `T*K*I2`), [`L134-L137`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L134-L137) (`grug_moe_dispatch_output`, `T*K*D`)
  - JAX-portable variant: flip remat policy so `grug_moe_dispatch_input` is recomputed from `(x, token_ids_sort)` instead of saved. Mirrors SonicMoE's save-indices-recompute-gather pattern. Pure JAX, measurable today.
- **gather-and-sum vs scatter-first aggregation**
  - scatter-first sites: [`L140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L140) `at[token_dispatch].add` (local) and [`L429-L432`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L429-L432) `at[token_local].add` + `psum_scatter` (ring-EP)
  - gather-and-sum reference already in tree: [`L218-L230`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L218-L230) `_unpermute_from_global_expert` `einsum("tkd,tk->td")`. Probe: swap the local scatter-add for a gather-and-sum unpermute on the same EP4 cell #3420 used.
- **`w13` / `w2` layout handling**
  - shapes pinned at [`L116-L117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L116-L117) (`moe_w13: [E D I2]`, `moe_w2: [E I D]`). #3821 / #4406 already explored padded `w13`; reuse those harnesses.

Out of scope for first tranche (CUDA-specific): Torch custom ops, Triton/CuTeDSL kernels, QuACK interfaces, Hopper/Blackwell async-store details.

# Constraints from prior negative results

- #3420 — local `scatter-add` is the durable TPU hotspot, but every Python/JAX return-path rewrite tested regressed against `scatter_psum_scatter` (2.069M tok/s on EP4 `v5p-8`). A gather-and-sum probe must measure on that exact cell or it is not credible.
- #4427 — post-#4297 H100x8 residual is communication/synchronization, not local FC1; SonicMoE's gather-fused GEMM targets local FC1, so the GPU win window on the `262144` cell is narrow (Triton at `26.1M tok/s`, Megatron forward at `33.1M tok/s`). Memory-side wins are the larger lever.
- #3431 — fused TPU forward kernel sat ~7.4x behind XLA. Do not redo any fused-forward kernel without a fundamentally different starting point.

# Proposed first benchmark tranche (pure-JAX, benchmark-only)

All on the existing Grug benchmark harness used in #3420 and #4427.

1. **Activation-memory remat policy probe.** Keep current scatter-first path; flip remat on `grug_moe_dispatch_input` (save→recompute), then on `grug_moe_dispatch_output`. Measure peak HBM and tok/s on EP4 `v5p-8` (#3420 cell) and H100x8 `262144` (#4427 cell). Stop if no peak-HBM reduction at iso tok/s ≥ -2%.
2. **Gather-and-sum unpermute swap on the local return path.** Replace [`L140`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L140) with a `_unpermute_from_global_expert`-style gather+einsum. Same two cells. Stop unless ≥ +0.5% over `scatter_psum_scatter` baseline on TPU EP4 and ≥ +0.5% on H100 exact-cap.
3. **Gather-fused FC1 probe.** Drop explicit `x_sort` materialization at [`L102-L108`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L102-L108); pass indices through a wrapper around `ragged_dot`. Measure on H100x8 `262144` (vs `triton` = `26121235.17 tok/s` from #4427). Stop unless ≥ +3% at parity HBM — #4427 already says local-FC1 headroom is small.
4. **`w13` / `w2` layout sweep.** Only if (1)–(3) leave a gap; replay #3821-style padded `w13` on top of the post-#4297 baseline. #4406 said this no longer adds lift on the shared exact-cap surface, so this rung is contingent.

Whole-scout stop: if (1)–(3) give no measurable win at parity HBM/throughput on either cell, seal as negative and do not escalate to custom-call / Triton / Pallas.

# Open questions for the human

- Confirm the canonical cells: #3420 EP4 `v5p-8` and #4427 H100x8 `262144`, or a newer authoritative cell?
- Gather-and-sum probe scope: local non-EP only, or also the ring-EP return path (where `psum_scatter` still must happen)?
- For the remat policy probe, is the user-visible knob a JAX `checkpoint_policy` or a Grug-level config that should select the policy at the model layer?

🤖 Update: honest remat and activation+W13 fusion both sharpen the current SonicMoE gap.

Scope: 1x GH200 on CoreWeave RNO2A, local full MoE shape `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, `topk=2`, BF16. Confidence: `exploratory`, but the negative result is decisive for this Pallas/Triton fusion shape.

Current comparison point:

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| `remat_bwd` / checkpoint | `4.798ms` | `5.844ms` with `prevent_cse=True` | `+21.8%` |

Important correction: the earlier JAX `remat_bwd=4.056ms` number used `jax.checkpoint(..., prevent_cse=False)`, so XLA could reuse work across the checkpoint. I changed the harness to `prevent_cse=True`; the honest forced-recompute result is `/dlwh/sonicmoe-jax-remat-prevent-cse-20260513-173642`:

| Backend | `prevent_cse=True remat_bwd` |
| --- | ---: |
| `scatter` | `5.950ms` |
| `sonic_xla` | `5.919ms` |
| `sonic_pallas` | `5.844ms` |

Real Sonic comparison jobs:

- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-real-forward-probe-20260513-172328`: forward `1.260ms`
- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-full-block-decomp-20260513-003600`: `fwd_bwd 3.428ms`, `fwd2_bwd 4.428ms`
- `/dlwh/sonicmoe-real-remat-successenv-20260513-172510`: `remat_bwd 4.798ms`

I also tried fusing activation-gradient derivation into W13 backward in Pallas/Triton:

| Backend/config | Steady |
| --- | ---: |
| `activation_w13_bwd_materialized_with_xscatter`, row 128 / k 64 / hidden 128 | `1.836ms` |
| `activation_w13_bwd_fused`, row 128 / k 64 / hidden 128 | `29.361ms` |
| split fused `dx` scatter | `14.129ms` |
| split fused `dw` | `15.318ms` |
| hybrid materialized gradient + direct `dx` scatter | `1.740ms` vs `1.839ms` baseline |

Jobs: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-smoke-20260513-185934`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-smoke2-20260513-190102`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-fused-full-20260513-190204`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-split-full-20260513-190356`, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-activation-w13-hybrid-full-20260513-190623`.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `fwd_bwd` | `4.199ms` | `4.336ms` | `12.804ms` |
| `fwd2_bwd` | `5.967ms` | `5.571ms` | `14.236ms` |
| `remat_bwd` | `5.953ms` | `5.792ms` | `14.430ms` |

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: Sonic/QuACK down-projection backward is a credible custom-call target; the Torch/DLPack bridge is only an ABI/timing proof.

I added `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_down_bwd_bridge_bench.py`, a focused harness for the Sonic `_DownProjection.backward` hot section:

- `_down_projection_backward_act(...)`, backed by QuACK `gemm_dgated`, computes `dh`, router-score gradients, and the weighted post-activation operand `a_prime`.
- QuACK `gemm(dout.T, a_prime, cu_seqlens_k=..., A_idx=...)` computes `dw2`.
- Inputs can be Torch-owned or JAX-owned and converted zero-copy to Torch through DLPack.

Full Grug local shape on 1x GH200, `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `intermediate=3072`, `experts=8`, top-2, BF16:

| Source | Steady |
| --- | ---: |
| Torch-owned tensors | `1.161ms` |
| JAX-owned tensors via zero-copy DLPack | `1.008ms` |

Job: `/dlwh/sonicmoe-down-bwd-bridge-20260513-202747`.

I also fixed the tiny correctness smoke. The first check compared against the wrong GLU layout: Sonic's default preactivation buffer is interleaved `gate0, up0, gate1, up1, ...`, not concatenated `[gate..., up...]`. After fixing the reference, `/dlwh/sonicmoe-down-bwd-bridge-ref4-20260513-133235` succeeded with BF16/accumulation-order scale diffs:

| Grad | max abs | mean abs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `dh` | `0.5` | `0.00547` |
| `dw2` | `0.125` | `0.01057` |
| `ds` | `1.845` | `0.324` |

The `ds` diff is still the least clean because the PyTorch reference reduces score gradients in a different order from QuACK's colvec-reduce path, but this is no longer the previous layout-scale mismatch.

Why this matters: the bridge bucket is roughly the same conceptual region as the JAX `combine_bwd + w2_bwd + activation_bwd` pieces (`~1.495ms` from the earlier decomposition), so the measured `~1.0ms` QuACK path is a plausible `~0.49ms` win candidate. That is large enough to matter for the remaining no-remat and honest-remat gaps.

Custom-call viability readout:

- QuACK's `gemm_dgated_tuned` and `gemm_tuned` each populated one autotuner cache entry after the call.
- QuACK compiles CuTe DSL kernels with TVM-FFI enabled and persists exported `.o` files via `compiled_fn.export_to_c(..., function_name="func")`; later runs load them via `cute.runtime.load_module(..., enable_tvm_ffi=True)`.
- The DLPack/Torch bridge is not a production JAX training solution because it is outside JIT and depends on Python/Torch runtime ownership.
- The production route should be either a source-level CuTe DSL port callable from JAX with `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call`, or an XLA FFI handler that launches the QuACK TVM-FFI/exported object code on JAX's CUDA stream. A larger whole-backward custom call may be needed if per-subkernel FFI overhead repeats the earlier isolated-gather custom-call tax.

Research logbook updated under `SONIC-PALLAS-043` in `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Milestone update for the GH200 Sonic-equivalent JAX path (`SONIC-PALLAS-046`, logbook: `.agents/logbooks/sonicmoe-pallas-grug.md`).

Shape/hardware: `T=8192,H=2048,I=3072,E=8,topk=2,BF16` on `coreweave-rno2a` GH200.

Current comparison:

| Path | Forward | `fwd_bwd` | honest remat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Real Sonic/QuACK | `1.260ms` | `3.428ms` | `4.798ms` |
| Previous best JAX/Grug | `1.285ms` | `4.035ms` | `5.844ms` |
| JAX + CuTe QuACK down-bwd (`sonic_xla_cutlass_down`) | `~1.285ms` | `3.998ms` | `5.103ms` |

What changed:
- The source-level `cutlass.jax.cutlass_call` port of QuACK down-backward is full speed in isolation: `0.956ms` for `dgated + dw2` at the full shape.
- The first whole-MoE custom VJP attempt was a negative result: `12.599ms` `fwd_bwd`, `14.048ms` `fwd2_bwd`, and remat hit `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`.
- The useful path is now granular: keep normal JAX/XLA dispatch, forward, and W13 backward, but wrap only `activation -> down ragged_dot -> gather_sum` in a custom VJP whose backward launches the QuACK CuTe calls.
- After setting `allow_cuda_graph=False` on the custom calls, `remat_bwd` succeeds at `5.103ms`. `fwd_bwd` remeasured at `3.998ms`, about `16.6%` behind real Sonic and inside the target band.

Open blocker:
- `fwd2_bwd` still fails with `Failed to set CUDA graph kernel node params: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` when the extra forward and custom-call backward coexist in one compiled graph. Disabling CUDA graph capture fixed remat but not fwd2, so this looks like a layout/alias/custom-call contract problem rather than ordinary dispatch overhead.

Interpretation:
- This is the first JAX-in-XLA path that reaches the desired speed band for backward/remat, but I would not call it production-ready until `fwd2_bwd` is stable.
- The remaining gap is probably not just JAX dispatch overhead. The isolated QuACK bucket is fast, but integrated savings are partly eaten by GLU interleave/deinterleave packing and residual XLA W13/backward scheduling.

Next steps:
- Inspect `cutlass.jax` `input_spec`/`output_spec`/layout controls and force the custom-call operands/results to match the CuTe views.
- Quantify full-shape GLU packing overhead directly.
- If layout fixes stabilize fwd2, keep this as the short-term JAX path; otherwise port the Sonic/QuACK W13 side or change the JAX W13 layout so the down-backward call consumes interleaved GLU activations directly.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up milestone: the speed blocker was mostly W13 GLU layout, not dispatch overhead.

Shape/hardware: `T=8192,H=2048,I=3072,E=8,topk=2,BF16` on `coreweave-rno2a` GH200.

Updated comparison:

| Path | Forward | `fwd_bwd` | honest remat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Real Sonic/QuACK | `1.260ms` | `3.428ms` | `4.798ms` |
| Previous best JAX/Grug | `1.285ms` | `4.035ms` | `5.844ms` |
| JAX + CuTe down-bwd, concat W13 | `~1.285ms` | `3.998ms` | `5.103ms` |
| JAX + CuTe down-bwd, interleaved W13 | `1.244ms` | `3.761ms` | `5.036ms` |

What changed:
- I measured the layout conversion tax directly: `concat -> interleaved` costs `0.315ms`, and `interleaved -> concat` costs `0.186ms` at the full shape.
- I added a benchmark backend that simulates storing W13 in Sonic's interleaved GLU layout. That lets JAX/XLA W13 produce interleaved activations directly and lets the QuACK down-backward custom call return interleaved `d_w13_out` directly, with no runtime pack/unpack around the custom call.
- Forward is value-equivalent to `sonic_xla` in the comparison job (`max_abs_vs_first=0.0`).

Interpretation:
- This reaches the original target on the meaningful measures: `fwd_bwd` is now about `9.7%` behind real Sonic, and honest remat is about `5.0%` behind.
- The remaining fwd+bwd gap is not mainly JAX dispatch overhead; it was mostly a layout mismatch around the Sonic/QuACK down-backward bucket.
- A real implementation should store Grug W13 in interleaved GLU layout, or use a Sonic/QuACK W13 path that naturally emits interleaved GLU activations.

Still unresolved:
- `fwd2_bwd` still crashes. Explicit `cutlass.jax.TensorSpec`, removing GLU pack/unpack, and disabling XLA command buffers did not fix it. With command buffers disabled, the crash moves to `wrapped_gather`, which points to a custom-call/XLA runtime correctness issue rather than the speed path itself.

Next concrete step:
- Prototype a real interleaved-W13 Grug layout path instead of the benchmark-only outside-timed transform, then keep fwd2/debuggability as a separate hardening task.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 jax-triton overhead update for Tri's pure-Sonic route:

What ran:
- Branch/worktree: `codex/sonicmoe-jax-triton-overhead` in `/Users/dlwh/.codex/worktrees/moe-jax-triton-overhead`
- Probe: `.agents/scripts/sonicmoe_jax_triton_overhead_probe.py`
- Platform: GH200 on `coreweave-rno2a`, JAX `0.10.0`, `jax-triton==0.3.1`, Triton `3.6.0`, Torch `2.11.0+cu128`
- Shape: `tokens=8192`, `hidden=2048`, `topk=2`, bf16, warmup 20, repeats 200

Key results:
- `jax-triton==0.3.0` did not work with our current stack (`CUDABackend.get_arg_specialization` missing). `0.3.1` works after forcing a non-empty `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` because the package was leaving it blank.
- Tiny one-kernel launch floor: direct Triton wall `0.0076ms`, jax-triton wall `0.0690ms`, delta `+0.0614ms`.
- Best standalone Sonic gather clone: direct same Triton body `0.0316ms` event / `0.0317ms` wall, jax-triton wall `0.1096ms`, delta `+0.0779ms`.
- `BH=2048 BK=2 warps=8` was similar: direct `0.0316ms` event / `0.0317ms` wall, jax-triton `0.1142ms`, delta `+0.0825ms`.
- Dependent tiny custom-call chain inside one `jax.jit` amortizes the fixed cost: chain length 1 `0.0726ms`, 4 `0.0767ms`, 16 `0.0963ms`, 64 `0.1990ms` JAX wall. The matching direct host-launched Triton chain goes from `0.0093ms` to `0.4243ms` wall.

Interpretation:
- Standalone pure-Sonic via `jax_triton.triton_call` does not beat the prior JAX-callable microkernel ceiling; it lands around `0.11ms`, like Pallas/FFI.
- The same Triton body is fast when launched directly, so this experiment points at fixed JAX executable dispatch for standalone microbenchmarks rather than obviously worse cubins.
- The chain result says per-custom-call overhead inside one compiled JAX executable is much smaller. So the path worth pursuing is whole-block amortization/scheduling/layout, not expecting a single gather microbench to match PyTorch/Sonic wall time.
- I would not add `jax-triton` to the production GPU extra yet unless we have a production backend that actually exploits the amortized whole-block path.

## Problem

When training over multiple epochs, the data is seen in the same order every epoch. The current shuffling infrastructure (`PermutationDataset`) applies a single fixed permutation and does not reshuffle on restart. There's an existing TODO for this:

https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/permutation.py#L19

This is particularly relevant for DNA experiments where we epoch over small datasets many times.

## Discussion

Some approaches were discussed here: [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1418673157585502370/1473412849916186735)

---
### Epoch reshuffling for multi-epoch training

- [x] Gather context: read current permutation code and related files
- [x] Understand the architecture and plan implementation
- [x] Implement `num_epochs` parameter in `PermutationDataset`
- [x] Update `EraShufflingDataset` to support epochs
- [x] Propagate `num_epochs` to `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` helper methods
- [x] Write tests (11 new tests + existing tests verified in diff review)
- [x] Run pre-commit ✅
- [x] Commit and push changes

### Summary

Added a `num_epochs` parameter (default `1`) to both `PermutationDataset` and `EraShufflingDataset`. When `num_epochs > 1`:

- The permutation operates over `num_epochs × dataset_len` elements
- Outputs are mapped back to the original range via modulo (`permutation(index) % dataset_len`)
- Each epoch sees all items in a different order — deterministic and resumable
- The reported `async_len()` is `num_epochs × dataset_len`

The `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` convenience methods on `AsyncDataset` forward the new parameter.

- `lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/dataset.py` — `shuffle()` and `era_shuffle()` methods
- `lib/levanter/tests/test_newdataset.py` — 11 new tests covering length, item coverage, reshuffling across epochs, validation, out-of-bounds, and convenience methods

**Testing:** Pre-commit (`./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files --fix`) passes cleanly including Pyrefly type checking. spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description

Evaluate whether June 67B context-extension checkpoints use retained MRCR conversation context when scoring the same final assistant response. The paired evaluator compares `full_context` with `query_only`, scores response-body tokens, and stratifies deterministic bootstrap intervals by needle count and evidence distance.

## Task

An MRCR source document contains two worked examples, a long multi-turn conversation with 2, 4, or 8 relevant facts ("needles"), and a final query. `desired_msg_index` identifies a user request in that conversation; its matching answer is the immediately following assistant message.

Each source row produces two documents with the same final query and gold response:

```text
full_context: two worked examples + target conversation + final query -> gold response
query_only:   two worked examples + final query                       -> gold response
```

The primary two-shot prompt supplies the benchmark's 10-character answer prefix. The evaluator scores only the remaining gold assistant response body. The worked examples, retained conversation, final query, supplied prefix, and EOS are context and receive zero loss. Each condition occupies one unsliced, unpacked sequence.

The paired comparison asks whether retaining the target conversation improves the likelihood of the identical response. Results report `query_only - full_context` NLL and BPB gain, with response-token micro and per-example macro aggregation, sliced by needle count and evidence distance.

### Difference from standard MRCR

Standard OpenAI MRCR gives the model the complete conversation, samples a response, requires the nonce prefix in that response, and grades the generated text with a `SequenceMatcher` similarity score. This experiment instead teacher-forces the gold response and measures its token likelihood twice: once with the target conversation and once without it. The supplied prefix is not scored. The resulting paired NLL/BPB gain is a diagnostic of context use, not an official MRCR generation score, and should not be compared directly with published MRCR scores.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Context gain (`query_only - full_context`) should move from non-positive before extension to positive after 64K/262K adaptation. Fixed qk=1.57 comparisons isolate checkpoint adaptation; qk=1.75 is the deployable final arm.

### Links

- [OpenAI MRCR dataset and task description](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d)
- [Research logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/babf963076/.agents/logbooks/paired-mrcr-base-eval.md)
- [Implementation snapshot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/63027b4e72)
- [Final qk1.57 W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mrcr-67b-step157000-qk157-cap262144-two_shot-v464cp8ep4)
- [Final qk1.75 W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mrcr-67b-step157000-qk175-cap262144-two_shot-v464cp8ep4)

## Results

Context gain is `query_only - full_context`, so positive NLL or BPB gain is beneficial.

| Checkpoint | qk | NLL gain (95% CI) | BPB gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| step 141000, pre-extension (8K) | 1.57 | -0.19453 [-0.21900, -0.16930] | -0.05789 |
| step 156000, 64K source | 1.57 | +0.40387 [+0.36399, +0.44537] | +0.12019 |
| step 157000, 262K extension | 1.57 | +1.18860 [+1.14205, +1.23597] | +0.35371 |
| step 157000, deployable arm | 1.75 | +1.26855 [+1.22432, +1.31342] | +0.37751 |

Each checkpoint used the same 299 paired source examples: 598 full-context/query-only condition sequences. Across four checkpoints, this is 1,196 paired checkpoint-example comparisons and 2,392 condition sequences.

Confidence is exploratory because each checkpoint received one evaluation pass over this dataset. One-shot/no-prefix and the full matrix remain untested.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Added a four-condition oracle-normalized measurement before rerunning the 299-example 262K slice.

The conditions form a 2×2 comparison: needles absent/present and distractors absent/present. `needle_only` retains all repeated target-request turns so the ordinal retrieval problem is preserved; `distractor_only` retains the complementary conversation turns. All four conditions score the same response-body tokens.

The headline recovery ratio is `(distractor_only NLL - full_context NLL) / (query_only NLL - needle_only NLL)`, computed as a token-micro ratio of aggregate paired contrasts. A 10,000-sample bootstrap resamples the same four-condition source tuples within needle-count and evidence-distance strata.

The ratio is identifiable only when the isolated-needle gain is at least 0.10 nats/token, its bootstrap lower bound is positive, at least 99% of bootstrap denominators are positive, and no denominator is zero. Before seeing results, the “good enough” gate is a recovery-ratio 95% lower bound of at least 0.80 plus a positive lower bound for distracted needle gain. Needle-count slices must each have positive distracted needle gain; distance slices are descriptive.

Implementation: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/5c32364665

Next: run the pre-extension checkpoint as a memory/artifact probe on `v4-64-cp8-ep4`, then run the remaining three checkpoints if it succeeds.
